title: Chicago's jazz scene and Stumpy Evans
summary: He lists musicians active in Chicago and says he never rehearsed.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But in Chicago there was a lot of activities, a lot of road bands, you know. Of course, as I said to you before, Dan, theaters and shows were the principal factors. You had Tiny Parham playing in Chicago. Fats was there. You had Earl Hines, Jimmie Noone, Teddy Wilson, Louis Armstrong. Jesse Stone had a band in one of the clubs, and Omer Simeon, you had a lot of the great guys and you had an opportunity to hear a lot of good jazz around. There was a guy named Stumpy Evans. Did you ever hear that name?

Tenor saxophone player. It was really great. Well I lived in a house with the people that he lived in. He was something else. But I could never understand how those guys could rehearse so much. 'Cause I never rehearsed, Dan. I imagine that's the reason why I didn't become a classical pianist. 'Cause you know, you gotta rehearse quite a bit, you know, well you just have to devote maybe two, three hours a day to, you know, to rehearse. Charlie Carpenter was there, the guy that wrote "Rosetta" with Earl, in Chicago.
